title: Unified Inference v29 — Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing (2028-10-12)
author: Asha Patel
abstract: This document bundles the product overview, PRD (requirements & acceptance criteria), high-level design, roadmap & themes, pricing & packaging notes, and release notes for Unified Inference v29. It summarizes goals, scope, success metrics, rollout plan, and migration guidance for customers and internal teams.
body:
Summary

This page describes Unified Inference v29 — the next minor release focused on two primary themes: 1) predictable cost improvements for high-throughput embedding workloads and 2) improved routing/resilience for multi-model fallbacks. v29 builds on the v28 platform performance improvements and introduces a new 'throughput-optimized' pricing tier for batched embedding customers, updated Console controls for routing policies, and a zero-downtime rollout plan for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Goals & Success Metrics

- Business goals:
  - Increase revenue from high-volume embedding customers by 18% ARR in 12 months through a targeted pricing tier and packaging changes.
  - Reduce support escalations related to model fallback by 40% after rollout.
- Product/technical goals:
  - 10% average token-cost reduction for embedding-heavy workloads (measured across top 10 customers).
  - 99.95% availability for hosted embedding endpoints (SLO).
  - Reduce cross-region fallback latency by 25% for cold-start fallbacks.
- Acceptance metrics (must-haves):
  - Batching/throughput profiles pass benchmark suite (p50, p95, throughput) on supported GPU types.
  - Console exposes routing policy controls and rollout toggles to customers.

User Personas & Primary Use Cases

- AI Platform Engineers (enterprise): need predictable per-month cost and SLA for embeddings index rebuilds and batch inference.
- Product Engineers (startup scale): prioritize low-latency search and moderate cost — will use hosted API with Optimize recommendations.
- Platform/Ops teams: require controls for routing policies and programmatic rollouts across Dedicated pools.

Scope (In-Scope)

- Backend: new batching scheduler tuning parameters, embedding-specific cache entry formats, routing policy extension in the control plane.
- Console: new UI for routing policies and a Pricing/Estimator page for throughput tier.
- Billing: support for a new throughput-optimized pricing SKU (monthly commit + per-embedding unit delta).
- Dedicated/Private: automated migration scripts and a canary plan for v29 agents.

Out of Scope

- Model architecture changes or new model families (no model training/finetuning).
- Major changes to REST API surface (we add optional parameters but remain backward compatible).

Requirements (PRD)

1) Throughput-Optimized Embedding SKU (MUST)
   - Description: New packaged SKU targeted at customers with high-volume offline/nearline embedding workloads (e.g., index rebuilds, bulk vectorization).
   - Functional requirements:
     - Support monthly reserved capacity with commit tiers: S (100k units/month), M (1M), L (10M).
     - Provide per-embedding unit pricing for on-demand above reserved commit.
     - Expose an estimator in Console that models avg batch size, throughput, and projected costs.
   - Acceptance criteria:
     - Billing correctly applies committed usage and overage rates in test accounts.
     - Estimator matches observed cost within 8% in trial customers.

2) Routing & Fallback Policy Controls (MUST)
   - Description: Allow customers to define routing policies (latency-first, cost-first, capacity-fallback) and configure fallbacks by model family/quantization profile.
   - Functional requirements:
     - Policy DSL in Console: simple toggles + advanced JSON editor for policy rules.
     - API: Add optional parameter routing_policy in generate/embed endpoints (string token referencing policy config).
     - Fallback behavior: automatic fallback to pinned compatible variant (e.g., lower-precision quantized model) when primary variant exceeds error or queue thresholds.
   - Acceptance criteria:
     - Policy changes take effect within 30s of save on hosted control plane.
     - Fallbacks trigger within SLO when thresholds are exceeded in load tests.

3) Batching & Cache Improvements (MUST)
   - Description: Scheduler and KV caching tweaks to reduce per-embedding token cost and improve throughput predictability.
   - Functional requirements:
     - New adaptive batching algorithm with workload-aware max batch windows per pool.
     - Per-model cache TTL and prefix-KV eviction policy tuned for embedding sequences (short sequences).
   - Acceptance criteria:
     - Benchmarks show >=8% throughput improvement for batched embedding replay workloads on A100 and H100 fleets.

4) Console UX & Rollout Controls (MUST)
   - Description: Operational controls for canary rollouts, per-customer routing overrides, and visibility into policy effect.
   - Functional requirements:
     - Canary rollout toggle with percentage traffic shift and automatic rollback thresholds in Console.
     - Per-route metrics surfaced: token cost, avg latency, fallback rate.
   - Acceptance criteria:
     - Internal teams can configure a canary and observe metrics; auto-rollback triggers in chaos tests.

5) Dedicated & Private Migration Plan (MUST)
   - Description: Provide day-2 ops scripts and a tested upgrade path for installed v29 agents.
   - Functional requirements:
     - Kubernetes manifests and Helm chart updates for agent v29.
     - Preflight check script that fails early for incompatible driver/kernel combos.
   - Acceptance criteria:
     - Zero-downtime upgrade demonstrated in staging for Dedicated pools with mixed model traffic.

Design Notes & High-Level Architecture

- New components:
  - Routing Policy Service (RPS): small control-plane microservice that persists policies and publishes diffs to edge routers.
  - Embedding Throughput Scheduler (ETS): runtime module inside serving runtime that exposes per-pool max_window_ms and dynamic batch shaping.

- Data flows:
  - Policy edits in Console -> RPS validates -> publishes to control-plane event stream -> Edge Routers apply rules and tag requests with routing_policy id.
  - Requests with routing_policy -> ETS uses policy hints (latency vs cost) to shape batch windows and select model variant.

- Backwards compatibility:
  - routing_policy is optional; default behavior remains the same. Existing customers see no change unless they opt in.

API & SDK Changes

- New optional request field: routing_policy (string) — accepted by /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings.
- Console exposes API key-scoped per-customer policy configs.
- SDKs (Python/Node/Go): add helper methods to create/validate policies and to call endpoints with routing_policy param.

Console & UX Mockups (high level)

- Pricing Estimator: input fields: avg batch size, qps, percent reserved usage. Output: projected monthly cost and suggested commit tier.
- Routing Policy Editor: top section quick-select (latency-first, cost-first, balanced), bottom section advanced JSON editor with validation.
- Rollout Controls: slider for percent traffic, metric thresholds, start/stop/cancel actions.

Roadmap & Themes (Q4 2028 -> Q2 2029)

- Q4 2028 (v29, targeted release 2028-10-12): throughput-optimized SKU, routing policy controls, console estimator, initial Dedicated rollout.
- Q1 2029: automated cross-region fallback (improved cold-start), model-variant recommendation engine in Optimize.
- Q2 2029: tighter integration with Redwood Optimize for per-customer quantization recommendations and post-deployment quality regression tracking.

Pricing & Packaging Notes

- New SKU: Throughput-Optimized Embedding (reserved commit model)
  - Commit tiers: S (100k units/mo), M (1M), L (10M).
  - Billing model: base monthly fee per tier + per-embedding unit on top for overage.
  - On-demand customers remain on existing per-embedding unit pricing.
- Migration incentives:
  - 3-month discounted trial on first commit for eligible customers (50% off month 1).
  - Engineering migration assistance offered for customers >$10k/mo with Dedicated contracts.
- Pricing rationale: reserved commitment enables larger batch sizes and better scheduler allocation, lowering unit cost and improving predictability.

Release Notes (v29) — Customer-Facing Highlights

- New: Throughput-Optimized Embedding SKU (reserved commit) — see Console > Billing > Estimator.
- New: Routing Policy controls to set latency/cost/capacity preferences and configure model fallbacks.
- Improved: 10% typical cost reduction for batched embedding workloads (observed in benchmarks).
- Improved: Canary rollout UI and automatic rollback thresholds.

Technical Release Notes (internal)

- Services changed: control-plane (RPS v1), serving-runtime (ETS v29), console (policy editor + estimator), billing (SKU support).
- DB changes: policy table (small schema add) — migration script included.
- Backwards compatibility: All APIs remain backward compatible. routing_policy param is optional.

Rollout Plan & Rollback Criteria

1) Internal canary (2 weeks)
   - Deploy to staging + 5 internal customers. Metrics: latency, fallback rate, error rate, cost delta.
2) Beta customers (4 weeks)
   - Invite top 10 embedding customers; monitor for regressions and estimator accuracy.
3) Hosted GA (gradual, 6 weeks)
   - Ramp traffic in 10% increments per week with automated rollback if error rate > 0.5% over baseline or fallback rate increase > 15% vs baseline.
4) Dedicated & Private (rolling upgrades)
   - Provide preflight script, run on subset of Dedicated pools, and then full roll.

Rollback triggers:
- Service-level error rate or new 5xx > 0.5% above baseline for 10 minutes.
- Fallback rate spike > 20% above baseline for 15 minutes.
- Cost estimator divergence > 20% against observed usage for pilot customers.

Operational Runbook (summary)

- Owner: Product -> Asha Patel; Engineering on-call rotation: Eng-Serving-Runtime (primary), Eng-Platform (secondary).
- Immediate actions for incidents:
  1) Identify whether issue originates from RPS, ETS, or Batch Scheduler via dashboard tags.
  2) If RPS: revert recent policy changes using policy-diff rollback.
  3) If ETS/serving runtime: scale pools to fallback variants and throttle non-critical consumers.
  4) If billing/estimator: temporarily disable estimator until patch validated.

Migration Guidance for Customers

- Hosted: opt-in via Console -> Billing -> "Try throughput-optimized SKU". No API changes required.
- Dedicated/Private: run preflight.sh, apply Helm chart v29, follow migration playbook in eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops.

Security & Compliance Considerations

- Routing policies are stored in the control plane and access-controlled via RBAC. Only org admins and users with policy-write permission can edit.
- Audit logs capture policy edits and rollout actions for 365 days (configurable via compliance add-on).

Open Risks & Mitigations

- Risk: Estimator inaccuracy due to wide variance in batch sizes per-customer. Mitigation: conservative default suggestions and post-signup trial period with human review for large commits.
- Risk: Fallbacks may change output quality. Mitigation: require customers to define quality guardrails per-route and integrate evaluation harness to track regressions.

Appendices

A. Acceptance Test Checklist
- Billing tests for commit tiers: pass
- Benchmarks on A100/H100: pass p50/p95/throughput thresholds - Policy apply latency < 30s: pass

B. Migration Playbook Links
- eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/preflight.sh
- eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/upgrade-and-rollback-v29
